dedupe_keys.name: noaa swpc satellite environment testbed exercise on space weather threats to satellite operations 2023

description: In October 2023 NOAA's Space Weather Prediction Center held its first Satellite Environment Testbed Exercise in Boulder, Colorado, bringing together space weather scientists, satellite owner-operators, tracking and manoeuvre service providers and commercial service providers to understand how satellite companies plan for and respond to space weather, and to assess NOAA's current and future products for the satellite industry. Over three days participants worked through a tabletop scenario modelled on a past Earth-directed coronal mass ejection and discussed operator actions and impacts. It covers low Earth orbit operations, where atmospheric drag was the biggest problem reported, followed by energetic particles in the radiation belts and solar storms; operators described losses from reduced satellite lifespan, replacement launches and more frequent manoeuvres for collision avoidance and orbit maintenance, recalling the February 2022 loss of 38 Starlink satellites. Outcomes were requests for better drag and radiation environment modelling, nowcasts, probabilistic forecasts and long-term predictions, event duration information and real-time data. The NOAA news article of 27 October 2023 is free to read; the exercise page on the testbed site returned 403 when checked. Caveats: the public account is a summary without the full scenario or findings report. It supports emergency response planning and hazard exposure analysis for satellite fleets during geomagnetic storms; related records are the Starlink February 2022 storm loss case and the 2026 bulk electric system exercise of the same testbed.
